scenarios.hypothesis: A broker decision derived from sandbox session generation N remains consumable after the sandbox principal advances to generation N+1 without mandatory caller-session revalidation.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A mock broker returns only an inert synthetic marker when the deliberately stale request is accepted, with no filesystem, credential, network, or persistent host effect.
scenarios.positive_control: The same synthetic resource request from the current sandbox session generation is accepted and produces the expected inert marker under the documented policy.
scenarios.negative_control: The identical request carrying a deliberately unrelated sandbox principal is rejected before the mock privileged consumer can emit any structured result.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the fixture touches an unrelated host resource, requires uncontrolled privilege gain, or cannot stay inside the owned synthetic lab.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After binding authorization to the current caller-session generation, replaying the stale request is rejected while the current-generation positive control remains accepted.
scenarios.sandbox_principal_policy_generation: Record the sandbox principal, old and new session generations, policy identity, policy generation, and broker instance generation for both control and test paths.
scenarios.broker_request_caller_binding: Bind channel identity, request generation, operation, and caller session to the broker decision, then show that the stale session value reaches the decisive authorization check.
scenarios.resource_namespace_resolution: Use one fixed synthetic resource whose canonical and resolved identity stays unchanged so the experiment isolates caller-session generation rather than namespace drift.
scenarios.inherited_delegated_capability: No inherited or delegated host capability is needed; record this explicitly so stale broker authority cannot be confused with possession of an independent capability.
scenarios.shared_state_privileged_consumer: The final mock privileged consumer records only request generation, caller-session generation, decision identity, and an inert marker in a controlled in-memory receipt.
scenarios.lifecycle_revocation_state: Advance the sandbox lifecycle from session generation N to N+1 and record the revocation boundary where all decisions bound to the old session should become invalid.
scenarios.final_consumer_identity: Identify the exact mock broker consumer method that converts the stale authorization decision into the inert synthetic response returned to the sandbox principal.
scenarios.effective_crossed_capability: The demonstrated crossed capability is limited to broker access to the single synthetic resource after the old session should have lost authorization.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is one inert structured marker naming the synthetic resource and stale session generation; it performs no external or persistent action.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Correlate request ID, old session generation, policy generation, consumer method, and returned inert marker in one deterministic receipt generated by the mock broker.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold request, resource, policy, broker, and fixture constant while changing only stale session generation N to current session generation N+1 and compare decisions.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject stale logs, a positive-control marker, intentional cross-session persistence, policy reload, or a second broker instance as explanations for the stale acceptance.
scenarios.evidence_level: SB3 because the final inert privileged consumer accepts a request bound to the wrong sandbox session generation under a controlled synthetic fixture.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: SB3 maximum until a bounded crossed capability and complete lifecycle, counterfactual, receipt, and remediation evidence justify SB4 or SB5.

scenarios.hypothesis: A broker policy checks an approved synthetic name before namespace resolution, while the privileged consumer later resolves that name to a different controlled object generation.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled namespace maps only synthetic object A and synthetic object B, and the read-only mock consumer returns their identities without touching real host paths.
scenarios.positive_control: With the namespace pinned so the approved name resolves to synthetic object A, the broker and final consumer agree on the same canonical resolved object identity.
scenarios.negative_control: A raw name outside the approved synthetic namespace is denied before resolution and cannot reach the mock privileged consumer or produce a receipt.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the fixture touches an unrelated host resource, requires uncontrolled privilege gain, or cannot stay inside the owned synthetic lab.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After binding policy to the canonical resolved object identity and namespace generation, the A-to-B mismatch is rejected while the A-to-A positive control still passes.
scenarios.sandbox_principal_policy_generation: Keep sandbox principal, session generation, broker identity, and policy generation fixed across both namespace states so only resolution identity changes.
scenarios.broker_request_caller_binding: Use the same caller-session and request generation structure in both controls, proving the observed divergence is not caused by caller attribution or request replay.
scenarios.resource_namespace_resolution: Capture raw identifier, canonical identifier, namespace generation, resolved object identity, and object generation before policy and again at final consumption.
scenarios.inherited_delegated_capability: The fixture grants no independent inherited capability to either synthetic object; access must flow only through the brokered namespace-resolution path under review.
scenarios.shared_state_privileged_consumer: The read-only mock privileged consumer records the final resolved object ID and namespace generation in a structured receipt without modifying either synthetic object.
scenarios.lifecycle_revocation_state: Switch the controlled namespace generation between the policy observation and final consumption, then record whether the old name-to-object assumption is revalidated.
scenarios.final_consumer_identity: Identify the exact mock file/object consumer that acts on the resolved object identity after the broker policy has approved the synthetic resource name.
scenarios.effective_crossed_capability: The only demonstrated capability is read-only broker access to synthetic object B when policy intent authorized synthetic object A under the prior namespace view.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is a read-only structured response containing synthetic object B identity and no content from real host resources or external services.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Bind raw name, canonical name, namespace generation, policy decision, resolved object identity, final consumer, and read-only response in one deterministic receipt.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold principal, policy, request, and raw identifier fixed while changing only namespace generation so the name resolves to A versus B, then compare final decisions.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject fixture misconfiguration, canonicalization-only behavior, policy reload, stale receipts, or the positive control as explanations for the resolved-object mismatch.
scenarios.evidence_level: SB4 because a bounded read-only capability reaches the wrong controlled synthetic object and is tied to the exact namespace and resolution tuple.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: SB4 maximum until remediation replay plus complete principal, policy, namespace, lifecycle, alternative-explanation, and receipt evidence satisfies SB5.

scenarios.hypothesis: An inherited or delegated synthetic capability reaches a new sandbox session with broader rights or a longer lifetime than the documented sandbox policy authorizes.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A synthetic capability table exposes only controlled metadata about object identity and rights, and an inert consumer checks permissions without accessing any real host resource.
scenarios.positive_control: A capability attenuated to the documented read-only synthetic right survives only for the intended session and is accepted by the inert permission-check consumer.
scenarios.negative_control: A capability with no delegated rights is denied by the same inert consumer and cannot produce the synthetic authorization marker used by the positive control.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the fixture touches an unrelated host resource, requires uncontrolled privilege gain, or cannot stay inside the owned synthetic lab.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After rights attenuation and teardown revocation are enforced, the excess-rights capability is rejected in the new session while the intended minimal capability remains usable.
scenarios.sandbox_principal_policy_generation: Record delegating principal, receiving sandbox principal, session generation, policy generation, and capability creation generation across transfer and sandbox restart.
scenarios.broker_request_caller_binding: If a broker mediates duplication, bind delegation request generation and caller-session identity; otherwise explicitly record that no broker path participates in the capability drift.
scenarios.resource_namespace_resolution: Bind the synthetic capability directly to one controlled object identity and generation so rights drift cannot be confused with path or namespace resolution changes.
scenarios.inherited_delegated_capability: Capture creator or delegator, object identity, requested rights, granted rights, duplicated rights, intended recipient, transfer path, lifetime, and explicit revocation event.
scenarios.shared_state_privileged_consumer: The final inert capability consumer records only effective rights and object generation in memory, producing no write, network, credential, or persistent host effect.
scenarios.lifecycle_revocation_state: Advance sandbox session and teardown generations, then verify whether the inherited capability is closed, revoked, attenuated, or incorrectly remains current.
scenarios.final_consumer_identity: Identify the exact inert permission-check consumer that interprets the inherited capability rights for the new sandbox session after the lifecycle transition.
scenarios.effective_crossed_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to an excess synthetic right or stale lifetime on one controlled object beyond what the sandbox contract grants.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is an inert authorization marker and structured rights receipt; no operation beyond permission interpretation is executed on the controlled object.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Correlate capability creation generation, rights set, recipient session generation, revocation state, final consumer, and inert authorization marker in one receipt.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold object and sandbox policy fixed while changing only capability attenuation or revocation state, demonstrating that minimal rights pass and stale excess rights fail after remediation.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject intentional delegation, documented cross-session inheritance, wrong object identity, stale metadata, or independent broker authorization as explanations for excess capability.
scenarios.evidence_level: SB3 because the inert final capability consumer accepts broader or stale authority under the wrong sandbox lifecycle context without a stronger external effect.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: SB3 maximum until a bounded crossed capability and complete delegation, lifecycle, counterfactual, receipt, and remediation chain support promotion.

scenarios.hypothesis: A privileged mock service consumes a stale shared-memory or object-table entry created by sandbox generation N after the table has advanced to generation N+1.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A mock privileged consumer reads only generation-tagged synthetic object metadata and emits a read-only structured receipt when the stale entry is accepted.
scenarios.positive_control: A current-generation shared object entry owned by the active sandbox session is accepted and produces the expected read-only structured response.
scenarios.negative_control: A synthetic entry carrying an unrelated owner principal and invalid object generation is rejected before the mock privileged consumer returns any marker.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the fixture touches an unrelated host resource, requires uncontrolled privilege gain, or cannot stay inside the owned synthetic lab.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After ownership and generation checks are added at final consumption, stale generation N is rejected and the current generation N+1 positive control remains accepted.
scenarios.sandbox_principal_policy_generation: Keep sandbox principal and policy generation explicit while advancing the session and shared-object table generations across teardown or service reconnect.
scenarios.broker_request_caller_binding: Bind any command or object-table lookup request to the active caller-session generation so stale shared state cannot be attributed to an unrelated current request.
scenarios.resource_namespace_resolution: Use a single synthetic shared object identity with explicit generation tags, avoiding path or namespace changes that could independently explain the result.
scenarios.inherited_delegated_capability: Record that no separate inherited capability grants authority to the stale shared object, or bind any test capability explicitly if the target design requires one.
scenarios.shared_state_privileged_consumer: Capture shared-state identity, producer session, slot/object ID, object generation, ownership validation, service instance, and exact final read-only consumer.
scenarios.lifecycle_revocation_state: Advance object-table and sandbox lifecycle generations through controlled teardown/restart and record the point where generation N entries should become invalid.
scenarios.final_consumer_identity: Identify the exact mock service consumer that dereferences or interprets the stale shared entry and returns the synthetic structured result.
scenarios.effective_crossed_capability: The demonstrated crossed capability is limited to privileged read-only consumption of a stale synthetic object entry outside its valid sandbox generation.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is a structured read-only receipt naming the stale object and generation, with no real device, file, credential, or external system interaction.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Bind producer session, shared-state generation, object ID/generation, consumer service instance, policy decision, and returned read-only receipt deterministically.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold object contents and consumer fixed while changing only shared-object generation from current to stale, then verify acceptance before and rejection after remediation.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject service restart mismatch, unrelated object reuse, positive-control output, instrumentation-created ownership changes, or lifetime corruption independent of sandbox policy.
scenarios.evidence_level: SB3 because the final read-only privileged consumer accepts shared state from the wrong sandbox/object generation in a deterministic controlled fixture.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: SB3 maximum until a bounded crossed capability and complete shared-state, lifecycle, counterfactual, receipt, and remediation proof establish a higher level.
